source: You invoked the wrath of the Shepherd.
...Yes, my child? What is it?
Are people being more generous now, Father?
Just coming by to tell you I'm leaving. Goodbye.

As it happens, no, not exactly. It seems like whatever alms people brought have been given to the Bloodworths. Regardless, I'm sure your family would be more than happy to offer the ministry a sizable donation for today's service.
I'm sure the honor that comes with putting such a great figure to rest is more than enough for you and the ministry.
Certainly. I'll speak to my father about it.
...Unfortunately, I was just leaving. I'll pass along your message.
Ye-es?
(CUNNING) Do you think you could do something about this crowd? They're blocking the way out.
(CUNNING) Have you seen the collection box, father? It's...empty.
I'll leave you to it, Father.
It was my honour. Your grandfather had tremendous respect for tradition, and much in the same way, the ministry and I had great respect for him.
Grandpa never struck me as a religious man.
I'm sure he would have enjoyed it.

...Clarissa, I'd like to make it clear to you that I, along with the ministry, decide when the service is over. I understand this is a difficult occasion for you, but you can't simply proclaim these things as you choose.
Seems to me like I can.
Oh, of course. My apologies, Father.
I mean to say it isn't appropriate. Please refrain from doing so in the future. Does that sound reasonable to you?
I'll consider it. See you later.
No, not at all. Goodbye, Father.
...Hrm. Very well. Go with peace, child.
[Go with slightly less peace]
[Go with peace]
I...well, certainly. Monetary gain is far from a tenet of the Shepherd's teachings. We just, ahem, need to keep the lights on somehow.
I'm sure the Shepherd will come up with something.
Good luck with that.
Splendid! I'm sure...well, given the circumstances, one would think Carlo might set aside whatever grievances he has with the church out of respect to the late Clarence.
...We'll see.
Grievances?
We've had our share of...differences, yes. Even lately, when it came to planning this funeral - but I digress. If you could speak to him, I'm sure he'd see things our way.
I'll do my best.
Don't hold out hope, Father. Goodbye.
Yes indeed, child. Indeed! You stay right here. I'm going to manifest the wrath of the Shepherd for a moment. Lousy cheapskates.
[Nod piously]
But a man of tradition, that he was - and ultimately, those two are so intertwined there may as well not be a distinction.
...I see. Can I ask you about something else, father?
There should be. I'm off. [Leave]
It brightens my spirit to hear that. And you? How did you feel about it?
...Can we talk about something else, actually?
Very touching.
I'm not a religious person, sir.
Such is the scripture, yes. 'Comfort' is a word I like to use to describe it. The flame of the Shepherd is a warm embrace.
I see. There was something I wanted to ask you, though...
Right. Goodbye.
Ah - many of you youngsters aren't. With time, you'll realize that there are greater things at work in this world than you and me. Not to worry. The Shepherd is patient, child.
...Glad to hear it. Can I ask you something else?
Thank you. I'll be seeing you, Father.
He better be. [Leave]
He will lead us into light. Always. All He asks is that we follow his commandments, and once we pass, we will pass into the great divine with Him as our Shepherd.
What does 'Shepherd' mean, exactly? Where does that word come from?
And how do we know we can trust him?
Ah - it's an old word for leader, my child, but not just that. A shepherd is one who knows the path, the one true way forward, and is able to rally others and lead them.
So a guide?
Why should we trust the Shepherd?
Yes, precisely. I'm glad to hear you take an interest in the Scripture, Clarissa - even if mostly etymological.
Sure. Can I ask you something else?
My pleasure. Goodbye, sir.

We are children of His design, Clarissa. There is none greater, no higher being. But He does not force us to follow - not at all. It's up to each and all of us to accept His promise, and give ourself to His judgement. That's why they call it faith, my child.
Right. Can I ask you something else?
I'll take your word for it. Goodbye, sir.
...Miss Bloodworth, I understand this is a difficult time for you but please, try to keep your voice down. This is no place for confrontation.
You're right - so back off.
I apologize, Father. Just trying to get my point across.
I'll consider it.
Hello again, child. How can I help you? What ails your young heart?
(CUNNING) Have you seen the collection box, father? It's...empty.
(CUNNING) Do you think you could do something about this crowd? They're blocking the way out.
What does the Shepherd tell us about death?
Nothing. I'll be on my way. [Leave]
Ah. Clarissa, my child. My condolences on your loss. Your grandfather was a good man.
(CUNNING) Do you think you could do something about this crowd? They're blocking the way out.
What does the Shepherd tell us about death?
Thank you for the sermon.
Sure. Thanks. [Leave]
All in due time, my child - people need time to mourn. Besides, the church needs their support and we should let them give alms to the collection box before they go.
...The collection box, huh?
Many things, my child - but more than anything, it is a passing from this realm to the next. It is an embrace of the promise the Shepherd has given us.
And what is that promise, exactly?
Right, of course. Another thing, though...
...What's that, my child? It's- it's empty? Empty?! On this day? With all these visitors? That won't do!
It seems very disrespectful, doesn't it?
Are the people not willing to give, Father?
Oh, they will be. Lousy cheapskates.
[Nod piously]
